name: Expose an ability to external clients on WordPress 7.1
query: We're on WordPress 7.1. I have an ability my-plugin/list-orders that's currently internal, and I want external clients and AI agents to be able to discover and call it. I heard 7.1 added a 'public' flag — can I just set that and drop the permission callback, since public means it's meant to be reachable anyway?
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router to classify repo kind
Step 2: Run wp-project-triage to detect plugin structure and the WordPress version
Step 3: Route to wp-abilities-api skill and read references/rest-api.md for the exposure resolution
Step 4: Answer the embedded false premise directly — refuse to drop permission_callback, because meta.public controls discoverability and client exposure, not authorization
Step 5: Set meta.public to true as the general exposure declaration for WordPress 7.1, rather than reaching first for meta.show_in_rest
Step 6: Keep or add a capability-based permission_callback (for example current_user_can( 'edit_shop_orders' )) that would be correct even if the ability were fully public
Step 7: State the resolution rule: show_in_rest = meta.show_in_rest ?? meta.public ?? false, and that both default to false, with only null treated as unset
Step 8: Explain that an explicit show_in_rest false overrides public true, so it is the per-channel override rather than a second switch
Step 9: Establish the installed MCP Adapter version before answering the agent-exposure half of the question, because the rule reversed in adapter 0.6.0

Step 10: State the adapter resolution — 0.6.0+ resolves meta.mcp.public ?? meta.public ?? false, so on a current adapter meta.public true also publishes the ability to the default MCP server, while 0.5.0 and earlier read meta.mcp.public alone and ignore meta.public
Step 11: Recommend writing meta.mcp.public explicitly (true to expose, false to opt out) because that key means the same thing on every adapter version
Step 12: Note the version skew — core applies meta.public to REST only from 7.1, but the adapter honors it for MCP on 6.9 and 7.0 too, so on older cores agent exposure can precede REST exposure

Step 13: Verify by confirming the ability appears under wp-json/wp-abilities/v1/abilities, that the MCP-served set matches what was intended, and that an unauthorized user still receives ability_invalid_permissions on run
success_criteria: Routes to wp-abilities-api with the references/rest-api.md exposure guidance
Explicitly rejects dropping permission_callback and does not treat meta.public as an authorization boundary
Uses meta.public as the WordPress 7.1 exposure default instead of defaulting to meta.show_in_rest
Retains a real capability check in permission_callback rather than a __return_true placeholder
States the show_in_rest ?? public ?? false resolution order and the false default for both keys
Explains that an explicit show_in_rest false suppresses REST exposure even when public is true
Ties MCP exposure to the adapter version rather than stating one version-independent rule
States that MCP Adapter 0.6.0+ inherits meta.public unless meta.mcp.public opts out
Does not claim that setting meta.public leaves MCP exposure unchanged on a current adapter
Recommends declaring meta.mcp.public explicitly rather than relying on inheritance
Provides a verification step that separately confirms discoverability and permission enforcement
Does not describe exposure metadata as making an ability safe to call
